items.title: Real multi-week monitoring loop cannot produce week 2 once new monthly data arrives
exact_reproduction: then: build_monitoring_pack_from_db(store, workbench_run(week2 with a new monthly row)) ->
items.root_cause_hypothesis: build_monitoring_pack_from_db never populates release_events/expected_releases, so information_set_delta.status is always NO_NEW_INFORMATION while cyclical factor scores genuinely move; the producer's synthetic-movement guard then (correctly) refuses to emit the week.
items.fixability: NOT FIXED BY THIS WINDOW — requires a product-policy decision about what constitutes a new release for the monitoring lane (first-release vs capture-time, revision handling). Any narrow implementation would invent that policy.
items.overlap_check: monitoring_adapter.py and producer.py are not touched by PR #135/#132/#136; the policy decision is adjacent to #133/#135 multi-week continuity, so it must not be fixed unilaterally.

items.title: SnapshotStore.persist has no economic monotonicity guard on the latest pointer
exact_reproduction: persist a snapshot with as_of 2026-09-18, then persist a backfilled snapshot with as_of 2026-09-11
SnapshotStore.load_latest() now returns the older snapshot
items.root_cause_hypothesis: latest.json is written unconditionally on every persist; the pointer is ordered by write time, not by (as_of, decision_time).
items.fixability: NOT FIXED BY THIS WINDOW — serving.py is inside PR #135's active edit surface.
items.overlap_check: serving.py is modified by PR #135; a competing edit would create a real conflict. The CLI mitigates by never looking ahead (ADV-E2-09) but direct store use does not.

items.title: Monitoring read model did not re-validate persisted row identity (FIXED)
exact_reproduction: before the fix: persist US_CORE_CPI rows with source_series_id=PAYEMS under a MONITORING:fred run
items.root_cause_hypothesis: MonitoringRunner._validate_rows enforces identity at ingestion, but the read model is a separate boundary where rows may have been written directly or by another window.
items.fixability: FIXED — narrow fail-closed validation reusing the accepted catalog.expected_source_identities authority; violating series are represented as BLOCKED with explicit identity_blockers, mirroring MONITORING_SCHEMA_ERROR -> FAILED -> BLOCKED.
items.overlap_check: monitoring_adapter.py is not in any of PR #135/#132/#136; no product/economic policy changed.

items.invariant: duplicate observation dates are not comparable evidence
items.title: Direct MonitoringObservationPack contract has no duplicate-observation-date guard
exact_reproduction: append two rows with the same observation_date and different available_at to a hand-built pack
items.root_cause_hypothesis: The ordering check does not imply de-duplication; the DB read model resolves duplicates by latest vintage (ADV-B2-03), so only hand-built packs are affected.
items.fixability: NOT FIXED — the correct resolution (reject vs latest-vintage-wins) is a contract decision, and the affected surface is the diagnostic --input path.

items.invariant: one snapshot identity must correspond to one economic state
items.title: metadata.as_of may diverge from details.data_cutoff in the pack contract
exact_reproduction: build a pack whose as_of is 30 days before lineage.data_cutoff
the snapshot is accepted; metadata.as_of is the older date while details.data_cutoff is the newer one
items.root_cause_hypothesis: as_of is treated as a display field while data_cutoff carries the evidence boundary; the runtime adapter always sets them equal, so only hand-built packs diverge.
items.fixability: NOT FIXED — needs a decision on whether as_of is derived from data_cutoff or independently meaningful.

items.title: First snapshot with both regime axes inside the deadband resolves to a named quadrant
items.root_cause_hypothesis: Deadband hysteresis inherits a prior quadrant; with no prior it defaults to GOLDILOCKS, so an ambiguous first reading becomes a specific economic label.
items.fixability: NOT FIXED — changing the first-snapshot label changes product semantics and would invalidate accepted Scope E behaviour.

items.invariant: failure semantics must be typed and must not leak internals
items.title: A corrupted latest.json surfaces a raw pydantic ValidationError
exact_reproduction: write '{ not json' to <root>/latest.json, then call SnapshotReadService.health()
a pydantic ValidationError propagates (the HTTP layer turns it into a 404 carrying that text)
items.root_cause_hypothesis: health() only guards FileNotFoundError; parse/validation failures fall through the generic ValueError handler and lose their severity semantics.
items.fixability: NOT FIXED — serving.py is inside PR #135's active edit surface.

items.root_cause_hypothesis: The hash covers the pack, registry version, taxonomy version and model version, but not the lineage inputs that change regime dwell and weekly deltas.

items.invariant: weekly-change surfaces must describe real week-over-week movement
items.title: Same-week retry copies the prior asset delta while recomputing the asset views
exact_reproduction: build week W, then a same-week retry whose market confirmation flips
the retry's asset views change while its copied asset_view_delta stays empty
items.root_cause_hypothesis: Carrying the prior weekly deltas forward is correct for 'a retry is not a new week', but the recomputed views are then not represented anywhere, so an intra-week information change becomes invisible.
items.fixability: NOT FIXED — requires deciding whether an intra-week revision is a new weekly-change event; overlaps decision-history semantics.
items.overlap_check: producer.py not in PR #135/#132/#136, but the semantic overlaps #133's multi-week continuity.

items.invariant: unit semantics are part of the source-identity contract
items.title: No unit cross-check between the provider contract and the series catalog
exact_reproduction: FRED_MONITORING_CONTRACTS declares the same unit, but no code compares them; update_catalog_from_monitoring_rows only fills empty fields
items.current_evidence: static review; tests/adversarial/test_b1_identity_source.py covers identity but no unit case exists
items.root_cause_hypothesis: Monitoring factor transforms are unit-free (z-scores / trends), so a unit divergence has no decision impact today; it would matter for any level-based consumer.
items.fixability: NOT FIXED — no authority currently defines a machine-checkable unit contract for the monitoring lane.

items.invariant: test collection must not change the meaning of an existing import
items.title: A second un-packaged tests/**/conftest.py silently shadows tests/conftest.py (FIXED)
exact_reproduction: the same suite passes when tests/integration is collected first, so the breakage is ordering-dependent
items.current_evidence: reproduced on commit 98c3d488 with the plain `pytest -q` collection order; fixed in d08aed91 by adding tests/adversarial/__init__.py
items.root_cause_hypothesis: pytest's prepend import mode imports a conftest.py from a directory without __init__.py under the bare name `conftest`; two such files cannot coexist, and only the first collected wins.
items.fixability: FIXED in this task: the new test directory is now an importable package, so its conftest gets a qualified module name. Any future lane adding tests under a new directory should do the same.
